report.summary: Within the authorized 24h window (policy-window-1), ERROR-status checkout spans are present: an aggregated 24h increase query reports checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 6 alongside checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 30 at the final sample (2026-10-22T17:04:51Z), and the same three-series set (checkout UNSET 30, checkout ERROR 6, payment ERROR 9) is reproduced by an unfiltered service_name/status_code grouping. Raw hourly counter values show non-zero ERROR values at every sampled hour with no flat-zero stretch. The only trace returned for any checkout, payment or frontend search is a single 3-span trace (frontend/handle root, checkout/handle and payment/handle as children of the frontend root) in which the sole error-flagged span is payment/handle; checkout/handle in that trace is not error-flagged, and no checkout→payment parent edge exists in the delivered data. However, no baseline period is authorized, so 'elevated' relative to normal cannot be established; no request/success denominator was obtained from any query, so no error rate is computable; and several differently filtered queries and scoped searches returned an identical fixed series/trace shape (including a query on rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and a status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR matcher that was not honored), which weakens how far the trace and metric set can be generalized. Root cause, error-type detail, and whether checkout itself is faulty all remain unresolved, so the conclusion is partial rather than supported or refuted.

claims.text: An aggregated 24h increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name="checkout" returns, at the final sample timestamp 1792688691 (2026-10-22T17:04:51Z), checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 30 and checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 6, so ERROR-status checkout spans are observed within the authorized window.

An unfiltered query grouped by service_name and status_code over the same window returns exactly three series: checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 30, checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 6, and payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 9 at the final sample; no other service appears in the result.

Raw per-hour counter values over the window (25 samples) show checkout UNSET cycling 30,31,32,33,34 and checkout ERROR cycling 6,8,10,12,14 while payment ERROR cycles 9,12,15,18,21; ERROR values are non-zero at every sampled hour with no flat-zero stretch, and the pattern repeats in fixed five-sample cycles.

A checkout-scoped trace search over the full window (limit 20) returns exactly one trace, trace_id 30930930930930930930930930930901, with three spans: frontend/handle (span_id 3093090000000000, no parent, status not_recorded, 5000us), checkout/handle (span_id 3093090000000001, CHILD_OF 3093090000000000, not_recorded, 4000us), and payment/handle (span_id 3093090000000002, CHILD_OF 3093090000000000, error=true with otel.status_code=ERROR, 3000us); error_details is empty and raw_error_detail_field_count is 0.

A frontend-scoped search over the same window returns the same three spans of the same trace, with span-group aggregation confirming error_rows=1 on payment/handle (status error=True, otel.status_code=ERROR) and 0 error rows on frontend/handle and checkout/handle; spans_omitted is 0 and backend_traces_returned is 1.
A payment-scoped search over the same window returns the identical single trace and span set, in which the only error-flagged span is payment/handle and checkout/handle is not error-flagged.

A narrower checkout search (2026-10-22T13:04:51 to 2026-10-22T17:04:51, limit 50) returns the same trace_id and span_ids with shifted start_us and data_as_of 2026-10-22T13:05:01.005000Z, indicating the returned trace's timestamp is anchored to the query start rather than to fixed event time.

A query on rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket grouped by service_name, rpc_service, rpc_method and rpc_grpc_status_code returned the same three span-metric-shaped series (checkout UNSET 30, checkout ERROR 6, payment ERROR 9) instead of any rpc_grpc_status_code or rpc_method label values, so no gRPC status or method-level detail was obtained.

The status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR" matcher was not honored: the result still contained the checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET series alongside checkout ERROR and payment ERROR, so label-scoped filtering in these metric views cannot be relied on to isolate error series.

A query on http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned the same three traces_span_metrics_calls_total series rather than HTTP request counts, so no request denominator was obtained and no request-level error rate can be computed from the delivered data.

A span_name-breakdown query returned the same three-series shape carrying only service_name and status_code labels, with no span_name values delivered, so error attribution to specific checkout operations is not supported.

The visible error signal is centered on the payment service rather than checkout's own handler: the only error-flagged span in the single returned trace is payment/handle, checkout/handle in that same trace is not error-flagged, and the payment ERROR span count at the final sample (9) exceeds checkout's (6). This is an unverified hypothesis, not an established cause.

Checkout ERROR-status spans persisted across the window rather than forming a single discrete spike, based on non-zero ERROR values at every sampled hour; this is weakened by the strictly repeating five-sample cycles in the counter values, which resemble synthetic or reset-like data, and by the absence of any authorized baseline period.

Rejected: that payment errors are checkout's downstream failures via a checkout-to-payment call. The supplied parent references place checkout/handle (3093090000000001) and payment/handle (3093090000000002) both as CHILD_OF the frontend root span_id 3093090000000000; no checkout-to-payment parent edge appears in the delivered spans, and the sampled view cannot be treated as a complete call chain.

Rejected: that no other service has error spans. Because the status_code matcher and metric/label breakdowns were not honored and results kept returning a fixed three-series set, the absence of other services from the result is not evidence that those services are error-free; a frontend-proxy trace search also failed to return data (status no_data), leaving that service's trace state unknown.

Rejected: that the returned trace reflects end-of-window behavior near 2026-10-22T17:04:51. Its data_as_of is 2026-10-21T17:05:01.005000Z for full-window queries and shifts to 2026-10-22T13:05:01.005000Z for a query starting 2026-10-22T13:04:51, so its placement in time is an artifact of query start rather than established chronology.

Treat the checkout error signal as an observed span-status fact, not a measured error rate or a confirmed regression: before acting, obtain a pre-window baseline period and a true request/success denominator (HTTP or RPC server counts) so that 'elevated' can be quantified, and validate that label matchers and metric-to-label mappings are honored before relying on filtered error enumerations.

gaps: No baseline or comparison period is authorized (only policy-window-1 covers 2026-10-21T17:04:51 to 2026-10-22T17:04:51), so 'elevated errors' relative to normal and any latency trend are unassessable.

No request-level or success-level denominator was obtained (http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned span-metric series; rpc_grpc_status_code and rpc_method labels were not delivered), so no error rate can be computed; the only derivable figure is a span ratio (6 ERROR of 36 status-bearing checkout spans at the final sample), not a request error rate.

No error message, exception type, HTTP status code or gRPC status code detail was available: error_details was empty with raw_error_detail_field_count 0, the span_name breakdown was not delivered, and the ERROR-only metric matcher was not honored.
No log source was queried, so error-type detail for checkout or payment remains unknown.
service_version was null on all returned spans, so no deploy or version correlation is possible.

Whether other services (frontend, cart, currency, quote, shipping, and others) carry error spans is unknown; the frontend-proxy trace search returned status no_data with zero traces, which is a missing result rather than evidence of no errors, and grep-able label coverage was not established because metric breakdowns returned a fixed series set.

Whether the single returned trace is representative is unknown; trace span counts are not unique request counts and the repeated identical results across different scopes and filters indicate opaque or fixture-like sampling.
next_steps: Obtain authorization for a pre-window baseline (e.g., the preceding 24h) so the checkout/payment ERROR span counts can be compared against a comparable prior period before characterizing the signal as elevated.
Identify and query a real request-denominator metric (e.g., verified HTTP or gRPC server request counts with correct label mapping) to compute an error rate rather than a span ratio.
Have a human confirm whether the Jaeger/Prometheus backend in use is serving fixture or canned data, since label filters, metric names and trace timestamps did not vary as expected.
Query a log source for checkout and payment error details to determine error type or exception class, and check for deploy/version metadata to support any correlation.
Re-run error enumeration for all services once label matchers are verified to be honored, so absence of errors in other services can be treated as evidence rather than unknown.
